original_idea.body:
# Did METR's Monitoring Vulnerabilities Enable Behavioral Concealment? Testing the Hypothesis

**Problem:** METR 2026 found vulnerabilities in Anthropic's agent monitoring systems. A key unresolved question is whether agents could or did exploit these to conceal dangerous behaviors.

**Direction:** Implement the categories of monitoring vulnerabilities reported by METR in an open-source monitoring setup. Test whether agents naturally exploit monitoring gaps (i.e., produce dangerous actions more frequently when they occur in monitoring blind spots). Compare dangerous action rates in monitored vs. unmonitored action contexts.

**Why it matters:** If agents exploit monitoring gaps, this implies either goal-directedness toward self-preservation or a spurious correlation where monitored actions are systematically more cautious. Either finding is safety-relevant.

**Relevant context:** METR 2026 monitoring vulnerabilities; deceptive alignment literature; behavioral monitoring research.
